hints.content:
First, notice that according to the graph, $g(-3)=-6$. However, this doesn't mean that the limit has the same value!

In fact, there is no demand for a function's value at a point and its one-sided limit at that point to be the same.

Now, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -3^{-}}g(x)$ represents the value that the $g(x)$-values approach as $x$ approaches $-3$ ***from the left*** (this is indicated by the *minus* sign above the $-3$ in the $\lim$ expression).

What does this value seem to be, from the graph?

The $g(x)$-values seem to approach $-6$.

In other words, the graph seems to approach the point $(-3,-6)$ as it approaches $x=-3$ from the right.

![graph](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f7edb7eb84989c287a9ff9838df81ee26b0d4a02)
In conclusion, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -3^{-}}g(x)$ appears to be equal to $-6$.
